test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A pair of shoes is sold by a retailer at a 20% discount on the marked price, but the retailer still makes a 28% profit on the cost price. What is the ratio of the marked price to the cost price of the shoes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relation between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) can be determined directly:

CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

CP / MP = (100 − 20) / (100 + 28)

CP / MP = 80 / 128 = 5 / 8

⇒ MP / CP = 8 / 5

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount on Marked Price = 20%

Profit on Cost Price = 28%

 
 
 CP: 100x

 
 
 SP: 128x

 
 
 MP: 160x

 
 
• 
 

 +28% Profit

 
 
• 
 

 -20% Discount

 
 MP : CP = 160x : 100x = 8 : 5

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the shoes be 100x.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100x + 28% of 100x = 128x

The retailer offers a 20% discount on the Marked Price (MP).

⇒ SP = MP − 20% of MP = 80% of MP

⇒ 128x = (80 / 100) × MP = 0.8 × MP

⇒ MP = 128x / 0.8 = 160x

Now, finding the ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price:

⇒ MP / CP = 160x / 100x

⇒ MP : CP = 8 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation Formula

CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This direct ratio relation helps solve markup and discount questions instantly without assuming variables.

Successive Discount

When two consecutive discounts D₁% and D₂% are given, the equivalent single discount is calculated as: D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂) / 100.

Markup Percentage

Markup percentage is always computed on the Cost Price to arrive at the Marked Price. Formula: Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100.
